title: Active learning identifies a high-performing four-metal perovskite oxygen-evolution catalyst
summary: A graph-based machine-learning model and closed-loop active-learning experiments identified a four-metal perovskite oxide with an intrinsic oxygen-evolution overpotential of 391 mV at 10 mA cm⁻²oxide, among the lowest reported for four-metal perovskite oxides. The study also reports recovery of several experimentally observed composition trends. This is an electrocatalyst material result; the abstract does not establish commercial electrolyzer performance.
ai_technology: Graph-based machine-learning model with active learning and closed-loop experimentation
organization: Institute for Basic Science; Seoul National University; Allchemy, Inc.; Polish Academy of Sciences; Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology

evidence.tested: A graph-based machine-learning model and closed-loop active-learning experiments identified a four-metal perovskite oxide with an intrinsic oxygen-evolution overpotential of 391 mV at 10 mA cm⁻²oxide, among the lowest reported for four-metal perovskite oxides.
evidence.unknown: The 391 mV figure is the reported intrinsic overpotential at 10 mA cm⁻²oxide and is compared by the authors with four-metal perovskite oxides. This is a material-level electrocatalysis measurement, not a commercial device result. The reported finding is one selected composition from a model-guided campaign; the abstract does not provide a full uncertainty interval.
evidence.ai_role: The model incorporated structural-characterization data and guided iterative material selection in a closed-loop experimental workflow. The authors state that it identified the composition with the reported 391 mV intrinsic overpotential; laboratory electrochemical measurements established the catalyst outcome.
